assumptions: THIS INCREMENT (outbox half, 2026-10-19): src/modules/platform-kernel/domain/outbox/ (the CTR-EVT-001 envelope checker and builder; the outbox entry and consumer-ledger key decisions; the D6 provisional relay batch size in outbox-limits.ts; the outbox and consumer stable errors) and application/outbox/ (OutboxPort, PublisherPort and ConsumerLedgerPort; in-memory fakes that model the producing and consuming transactions; the relayOnce relay step; the consumeEvent replay-safe consumer), with their tests; plus Q0-301-1 (a direct holdsLease workspace test) and A1-301-I1 (the job fake refuses a repeated job_id); the manifest's outputs.files and one appended open_blockers entry.

The outbox follows 050_async_kernel.sql: an entry is a CTR-EVT-001 envelope at a position assigned at commit, and having been published is dispatched_at's nullability, never a status value; the consumer ledger's key is (workspace_id, consumer, event_id), the workspace being the event's own. The fakes model a transaction: what a unit of work stages (events, domain state, a ledger row, a consumer's effect) commits together when its work resolves and not at all when it rejects; a concurrent unit holding the same ledger key makes the second wait, as the unique constraint does.

Delivery is at-least-once: relayOnce marks an entry only after its publish resolved, and stops at the first entry it cannot publish or mark (A0's inference: order within a step; a permanently unpublishable entry holds the queue, a D6 question since CTR-EVT-001 names no event dead-letter). The relay batch size (50) is a D6 provisional test value, A0's inference.

An event carries only a minted tenant context (isMintedTenantContext) and its correlation_id; a unit of work refuses an event of another workspace; a mark must name the entry's position, event and workspace. Every outbox and consumer stable error code and message key is A0's inference; the consumer name is bounded at 64 as 050's consumer_ledger_consumer_bounded.

security_privacy_cost_impact: No provider, credential, network, data or cost. Security-relevant by design: an event carries only a minted tenant context and is appended only in its own workspace's unit of work; an entry is marked only by a reference naming its position, event and workspace; a consumer's ledger key is the event's own workspace, so one tenant's delivery neither suppresses nor reveals another's; a report or record carries ids and minted codes only, never a thrown or returned value's text; handler failures roll back both the ledger row and the effect. A1 reads it (risk lane). Fix round 1 (A1-302-1): every port, fake, relay and consumer decision now reads a frozen copy taken in one read of the caller's value, so a getter or proxy cannot pass the workspace or event-id checks with one value and store another.

compatibility_impact: Additive: new files under domain/outbox/ and application/outbox/, one test each added to job-decisions.test.ts and job-store.test.ts, and a refusal of a repeated job_id in the job fake (test-only code); nothing imports the outbox code yet (index.ts and run.ts unchanged). No contract-catalog, dependency or tool-configuration change.
known_limitations: The fakes model the transactions; the database adapter's equivalents (the outbox insert in the command's transaction, the ledger insert under its unique constraint, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for concurrent relays) are scope.exclude, so criterion 5 is shown on the fakes only and criterion 7 stays unmet.

Concurrent relays may each publish an entry before one marks it; delivery is at-least-once by design and the consumer ledger absorbs the repeat. A permanently unpublishable entry holds the queue (no event dead-letter in CTR-EVT-001; D6).
The relay batch size is a D6 test value; the per-round budget, concurrency and the Cron (Q-029-2) are the dispatcher increment's.
